original.target_description: Study 1 online experiment on organ-donation consent with opt-in, opt-out, and neutral conditions. Description names opt-out consent but does not identify a contrast; opt-out versus opt-in and opt-out versus neutral are both described. Supplied p.2 locator instead points to later country analyses.

n.sample_role: 161 respondents across all three conditions; candidate experiment total, not established analytic N for either opt-out contrast.
n.exclusions: No contrast-specific final group counts or exclusion details in supplied main article; supporting methods not supplied.

notes: Identity assessment: canonical text is a complete two-page primary Science Policy Forum article headed Do Defaults Save Lives?, authored Eric J. Johnson and Daniel Goldstein, with printed Science volume 302, 21 November 2003, pages 1338–1339. These match the neutral original reference; DOI is not printed in this text and was not independently verified. No PDF supplied. Study 1 is on printed p.1338, not supplied locator p.2. Candidate comparisons: opt-out versus opt-in (narrative about twice the consent rate), and opt-out versus neutral (not significantly different). Figure reports consent percentages 42 opt-in, 82 opt-out, 79 neutral; these are descriptive condition percentages, not a printed comparison effect size or odds ratio. No contrast selected from row order or numeric correspondence. Candidate N=161 is total across three conditions; no final group counts establish contrast analytic N. No N sum performed. Main text gives qualitative significance for Study 1; no numeric same-test p identified. Note 24 points to supporting methods/details not supplied. The p.1339 16.3% increase and P < 0.02 concern actual country-level donation regression, a different study/outcome, excluded from this target. Unassigned replication and success fields are placeholders.
